messages:
sanjay: Quick idea—build a 'Routing Inspector' trace API to surface a compact decision trace for each routing decision. Goal: make debugging and rollout diffs way easier without exploding logs. Sketching perf/privacy tradeoffs, looking for feedback. :eyes:

maria: Love the idea. Two quick Qs: how do we avoid 10x latency on hot paths, and what do we serialize (scores only? reasons?)

aj: Also: tenant privacy. We can't leak anything that could be correlated back to customer traffic in traces that are accessible to non-ent teams.

lex: Rough schema proposal (very compact):
```json
{
  "rid": "req-1234",
  "route": [
    {"step": "compat-check", "ok": true},
    {"step": "penalty-eval", "score": 12, "reason": "region-penalty"},
    {"step": "quota-pass", "ok": true}
  ],
  "variant": "rw-13b-q4f",
  "final_score": 0.92
}
```
Keep strings short, numbers only where necessary. No raw tenant ids in the payload (we can map to opaque tenant hash if needed).

devon: Policy for retention? We need TTL + automatic scrub for traces older than X. Also opt-in per-tenant detailed traces for enterprise customers.

ops-bot: FYI runbook pointers: https://redwood-internal/ops/routing-inspector (draft). Includes data classification notes. :link:

sre_ben: Implementation note: sample at gateway with configurable p (0.01 default). For sampled requests, annotate a tiny trace id and stream full trace into observability pipeline async. That keeps request path sync cheap (just attach trace-id header).

maria: That sounds reasonable. For debugging a rollout we sometimes want full traces for 100% of requests for a short window—how would that work?

sanjay: Two modes: 1) inline debug: enable full traces for a tenant or route via admin flag for N minutes (gateway returns trace inline), 2) sampled async: trace-id header + background ingest. Inline mode guarded by rate limiter + ACL.

aj: Encryption/KMS question: traces stored in observability should be encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Also scrub any potentially identifying path/query params before ingest.

lex: Agree. On the API surface, propose endpoints: POST /inspect/run (ad-hoc), GET /inspect/{trace_id} (fetch), and streaming hook to push to users' S3/Kafka. Use a small, versioned schema header so we can evolve trace shapes.

devon: Rollout plan thoughts: start with internal-only (dev & eng), then opt-in beta customers, then gradual on-by-default sampling. Add audit logs for who fetched a trace.

sre_ben: Perf numbers to aim for: inline overhead <= 0.5ms when tracing disabled, trace-id injection cost < 150us. Background collector should be non-blocking and retriable.

maria: For debugability we want diffing tools: compare decision_path between two builds or model variants. If trace schema is stable we can diff arrays of step stamps. Also include a digest/hash of request fingerprint to join with other telemetry (but hashed).

sanjay: Example use-case: canary shows higher cost on edge region—inspector shows penalty layer adding +20 to score and selecting higher-cost variant. We can then tune penalty curve. That saved time in my last postmortem.

aj: Security ops: require a per-tenant allowlist for inline traces, require justification metadata for audit.

lex: Small implementation detail: store only numeric scores and short reason tokens (enum ids). Keep human-readable reason lookup table elsewhere (secured). That reduces PII/size.

devon: Can we provide a CLI helper to fetch traces and open a local diff viewer? That would speed debugging for SEs.

sanjay: Yes — plan: inspector CLI + web UI in Console (internal first). CLI command: `rw inspect fetch <trace_id> --pretty`

maria: TL;DR approvals? I think this is worth prototyping. Need perf guardrails, sampling default, storage TTL, encryption, and tenant ACLs. :thumbsup:

sanjay: I'll draft an RFC with the schema, sampling model, rollout checklist, and security controls. Will ping owners for each bullet and include microbenchmarks. Thanks all. :party_parrot:

aj: +1 from security. Ping me on the RFC for threat model.

sre_ben: I'll add perf harness tasks to infra backlog.

lex: I'll convert the sketch into a proto and include example diff tooling notes.

ops-bot: Note: opened tracking ticket INF-2359 for initial prototype.
